title: Optimize CPU request path: thread pinning, serialization, and thread-pool tuning
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: production workloads hitting CPU-bound request paths showed high p99 latency and reduced throughput for small-batch/short-sequence requests. Root cause analysis pointed to three classes of CPU-side bottlenecks: (1) expensive per-request serialization/deserialization and many small syscalls, (2) contention and suboptimal scheduling in the shared thread pool, and (3) NUMA/cpu-migration overheads due to threads not being pinned. This PR implements a set of complementary changes to address these: 1) Introduce a fast-path deserializer using simdjson for the common JSON request shape and add an optional binary pre-parsed wire-format for internal clients to avoid repeated parsing, 2) Replace the single global worker queue with a tiered thread-pool (io, cpu-worker, kv-cache) with work-stealing disabled across NUMA domains, exposing config knobs for core assignments, max-workers, and per-queue batch sizes, 3) Add explicit thread-pin/affinity support and a NUMA-aware allocator for runtime hot paths, 4) Batch response serialization for continuous-batching flows to reduce write syscalls and copy overhead, 5) Migrate KV-cache maintenance tasks to dedicated pinned workers to prevent cache eviction jitter from application threads. Implementation notes: - All changes are behind runtime feature flags and default to conservative values for backwards compatibility. - New telemetry: runtime.thread_pool.active, runtime.thread_pool.queue_latency_ms, runtime.serialization.fastpath_hit_rate, runtime.kv_cache.maintenance_latency. - Config knobs exposed via the existing runtime config proto (fields added in runtime/config.proto). Checklist: - [x] Implement fast-path deserializer and wire-format fallback - [x] Implement tiered thread pool with affinity options - [x] Add NUMA-aware allocator and pinning utilities - [x] Add KV-cache pinned maintenance workers - [x] Add CI and perf benchmarks and run perf harness - [x] Add docs: docs/perf/threads.md and runtime config doc - [x] Manual rollout testing on dedicated cluster and canary. Impact/Results: microbenchmarks (continuous-batching small-batch scenario, batch size=1-4, seq_len=8-64) show 20-35% reduction in p99 latency and 10-18% throughput improvement under CPU-bound load; KV-heavy workloads saw reduced tail latency variance and up to 30% reduction in maintenance-induced latency spikes. No functional behavior changes expected when feature flags are off. Rollout: feature-gated; canary enabled in dedicated/staging for 48h before org-wide rollout. Related: ENG-1283 (threading perf), ENG-1297 (kv-cache stability).

release_notes: Performance: Reduce CPU-side request latency and improve throughput for small-batch/short-sequence workloads by optimizing serialization, introducing a tiered/pinned thread pool, and moving KV-cache maintenance to dedicated pinned workers. Exposed runtime knobs for affinity and pool sizing.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated by default. To enable in a cluster set runtime.config.threading.enable_pinning=true and tune runtime.config.threading.cpu_workers_per_socket. Monitor new metrics: runtime.thread_pool.queue_latency_ms and runtime.serialization.fastpath_hit_rate. Canary for 48h recommended.
